config_verbatim:
# The cell FINDINGS.md §7 asks for first: redstring's chunking, on the
# corpus that actually matters.
#
# ## Why this arm exists
#
# Everything measured on `prime-rel` so far is `whole-document`, chosen
# deliberately so the relations result would be a statement about the
# corpus and not about granularity. That choice worked -- and it means the
# best number this project has (`qwen-rel-whole` + rerank, 0.41948) says
# almost nothing about redstring, because redstring's chunker was switched
# off for it.
#
# This arm turns it back on. `qwen-rel-sliding1k` minus `qwen-rel-whole`,
# at a fixed model and a fixed corpus, is the cost or benefit of chunking
# the relations text.
#
# ## Why `sliding-1000-500` rather than `boundary-preference`
#
# `boundary-preference` came last on dense retrieval on Nemotron, on nomic,
# and on qwen's mini set -- three models, same ordering (FINDINGS §3).
# Re-testing a three-time loser on the good corpus is worth less than
# measuring the chunker that has beaten it every time. If sliding wins here
# too, that is a fourth data point and the diagnostic FINDINGS §3 asks for
# gets built instead of a fifth arm.
#
# ## The prediction worth writing down before the number exists
#
# The `- relations:` block sits at the END of each document, and the
# relations finding is that those neighbour names are what the lexical
# channel matches. A 1000-character window with 500 overlap therefore does
# something specific to this corpus that it did not do to `prime`: it
# **isolates the relations block into its own chunk** for the 19.5% of
# documents over 2,400 characters.
#
# Two outcomes are plausible and they point opposite ways:
#
# - Dense may IMPROVE. `qwen-rel-whole` dense moved only +0.004 over
#   no-relations, which was read as "a single vector compresses the
#   neighbour names away". If that reading is right, giving the names their
#   own vector should recover some of it -- and `aggregation: max` means
#   one strong chunk carries the node.
# - Lexical may DEGRADE, or not move. BM25 already sees every term in the
#   document whether it is one chunk or four; what changes is the length
#   normalisation and the per-chunk idf, not what is visible.
#
# If dense rises and lexical holds, chunking is worth its cost on this
# corpus and the §3 diagnostic has its mechanism. If dense does not move,
# the +0.004 has a different explanation and the compression story is
# wrong. Either way this is a cell whose result is informative, which is
# the bar an arm has to clear.
#
# ## Cost
#
# The embedding cache pays here for the first time on a real arm. Every
# document under 1000 characters yields a single chunk byte-identical to
# its `whole-document` chunk, so it is a guaranteed hit on the vectors
# `qwen-rel-whole` already paid for. Documents above the window are all
# misses. Measured cross-chunker hit rate on `prime-mini` was 44.7%
# (CLAUDE.md), and that is the number to check this run against -- an arm
# with near-zero hits is telling you the cache key is wrong, which nothing
# else in the report would show.
name: qwen-rel-sliding1k
dataset: prime-rel
split: test-0.1
chunker: sliding-1000-500
embeddings: qwen3-embedding-0.6b
dimension: 1024
aggregation: max
agent: dense
k: 20

# See `qwen-rel-whole.yaml`. The document side being empty is the correct
# value for Qwen3-Embedding, not an omission.
document_prefix: ""
query_prefix: "Instruct: Given a query, retrieve relevant documents that answer the query\nQuery: "

cost.ann_index_definition: CREATE INDEX kg_chunks_qwen3_embedding_0_6b_1e22db42_hnsw_qwen_rel_sliding1k ON public.kg_chunks_qwen3_embedding_0_6b_1e22db42 USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops) WITH (m='16', ef_construction='64') WHERE (tenant_id = 'ab815a67-af9a-52e4-a2e1-fc3bacfd77c0'::uuid)
